title: Real Madrid eject fan for allegedly performing Nazi salute before Benfica tie
content:
Real Madrid have opened disciplinary proceedings after a fan was caught on camera allegedly performing a Nazi salute before their Champions League tie against Benfica.

Madrid confirmed a supporter in the Grada Fan section, located in the south side of the Bernabeu, had been identified by security staff and ejected after footage emerged of him appearing to make the gesture before kick-off.

Unlike in other European countries including Germany and Italy, where a Nazi salute is considered a criminal offence, the gesture alone is not in Spain. It can, however, be punishable by law if accompanied by other acts which constitute a hate crime.

A large “no to racism” banner was displayed by Madrid fans as the teams lined up and the Champions League anthem played before kick-off during Wednesday’s tie.

Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni was serving a one-game provisional suspension for the play-off match while UEFA investigates allegations that he racially abused Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior during last week’s first-leg. UEFA said he had been suspended “without prejudice”.

In February 2024, a Chelsea supporter was given a three-year football banning order for performing a Nazi salute towards Tottenham Hotspur fans during a Premier League fixture the previous November.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed the fan was convicted of a racially aggravated public order offence.
